name: Mysuru Palace (Amba Vilas)
description: The historical seat of the Wadiyar dynasty, renowned for its Indo-Saracenic architecture, intricate stained glass, carved silver doors, and Sunday illuminations.
best_time_to_visit: October to March (Grand Dussehra in Oct)
cultural_note: Footwear must be deposited outside before entering the palace interior. Photography is permitted in designated halls.
must_try_food: Mysore Pak at Guru Sweets, authentic Mysore Masala Dosa at Mylari.
accessibility: Wheelchair ramps available on ground floor; battery-operated buggies outside.

name: Chamundeshwari Temple & Nandi Monolith
description: Perched atop Chamundi Hill at 1,000 meters elevation, dedicated to Goddess Chamundeshwari, featuring panoramic views of Mysuru city and the 16-foot monolithic Nandi bull.
cultural_note: Dress conservatively for sanctum darshan. VIP fast-track tickets available for INR 100 during busy festivals.
must_try_food: Fresh tender coconut (yele-neeru) stalls along the hill climb.
accessibility: Road goes directly to temple entrance; stair climb optional (1,008 steps).

name: Hampi Monumental Complex & Virupaksha
kannada_name: ಹಂಪಿ ಸ್ಮಾರಕಗಳ ಸಮೂಹ ಮತ್ತು ವಿರೂಪಾಕ್ಷ ದೇವಾಲಯ
description: UNESCO World Heritage site representing the capital of the 14th-century Vijayanagara Empire. Marvel at the stone chariot, musical pillars, and Tungabhadra riverbanks.
best_time_to_visit: November to February (Cooler climate for boulder exploration)
cultural_note: Active sacred shrine at Virupaksha temple; footwear must be removed inside. Coracle boat rides on Tungabhadra operate subject to water levels.
must_try_food: Traditional North Karnataka Jolada Rotti Oota (sorghum flatbread with brinjal curry).
accessibility: Electric buggies connect Vijaya Vittala parking to the Stone Chariot.

name: Badami Cave Temples & Agastya Lake
description: 6th-century rock-cut cave temples crafted by the Early Chalukyas into red sandstone cliffs overlooking the ancient Agastya Lake.
cultural_note: Cave 1 displays the 18-armed dancing Shiva (Nataraja) exhibiting 81 distinct Bharatanatyam poses.
must_try_food: Dharwad Peda & Badami Shengachutney (peanut chutney powder) with Jolada Rotti.
accessibility: Moderate stair climbing required between the 4 caves.

name: Raja's Seat & Abbey Falls
description: Misty viewpoints where Kodagu kings enjoyed sunsets, coupled with Abbey Falls cascading through coffee and spice plantations.
cultural_note: Support local coffee growers by purchasing single-origin Arabica/Robusta coffee directly from cooperative counters.
must_try_food: Kadambuttu (steamed rice balls) with traditional Kodava curries and bamboo shoot relish.
accessibility: Raja's Seat garden is paved; Abbey Falls has steps leading down to the bridge.

name: Dubare Elephant Camp
description: Eco-tourism site on the banks of river Kaveri where visitors observe elephant bathing, feeding, and learn about forest conservation.
opening_hours: 9:00 AM - 11:30 AM & 4:30 PM - 5:30 PM (Subject to seasonal river flow)
cultural_note: Operated by Jungle Lodges & Karnataka Forest Department. Strict animal welfare protocols apply.
must_try_food: Akki Rotti (rice flour flatbread) with coconut chutney.
accessibility: Requires short river crossing by boat or footbridge depending on water level.

name: Om Beach & Mahabaleshwar Temple
description: Iconic beach shaped naturally like the auspicious Hindu symbol 'Om', paired with the 4th-century coastal Atma Linga shrine.
opening_hours: Temple: 6:00 AM - 12:30 PM & 5:00 PM - 8:00 PM; Beach: Open daylight
cultural_note: Traditional dhoti required for male entry into the inner temple sanctum. Beach trek between Kudle, Om, and Half-Moon is a scenic trail.
must_try_food: Coastal Mangaluru/Konkan seafood, Neer Dosa, and fresh pineapple juice.
accessibility: Om beach parking has stair path descent to the sand.

name: Udupi Sri Krishna Matha & Malpe Beach
kannada_name: ಉಡುಪಿ ಶ್ರೀ ಕೃಷ್ಣ ಮಠ ಮತ್ತು ಮಲ್ಪೆ ಕಡಲತೀರ
description: Famed 13th-century temple established by saint Madhvacharya where Lord Krishna is viewed through the Kanakana Kindi window, coupled with Malpe's golden sand beach.
best_time_to_visit: August to March (Krishna Janmashtami celebrated with grand fervor)
cultural_note: Complimentary sattvic community meals (Maha Prasada) served daily to all visitors at midday.
must_try_food: Udupi Goli Baje, Mangalore Buns, and hot filter coffee at Mitra Samaj.
accessibility: Temple inner parikrama is wheelchair accessible on ground level.

name: Mullayanagiri Peak & Baba Budangiri
description: The highest peak in Karnataka at 1,930 meters, offering cloud walks, breezy western ghats ridges, and birthplace of Indian coffee cultivation.
opening_hours: 6:00 AM - 5:00 PM (Forest check-post entry restrictions apply)
cultural_note: Baba Budangiri represents shared syncretic Sufi-Hindu heritage. Drive carefully on narrow mountain switchbacks.
must_try_food: Estate-fresh filter coffee and Malnad Jackfruit chips.
accessibility: Vehicles reach the base; final ~400 steps paved to summit temple.

name: Jog Falls (Gersoppa)
description: The second-highest plunge waterfall in India, where the Sharavathi river splits into Raja, Roarer, Rocket, and Rani cascades plunging 253 meters.
opening_hours: 7:30 AM - 6:00 PM (Laser light show at 7:15 PM)
cultural_note: Viewpoints maintained by Karnataka Tourism (KSTDC). Descent to the bottom involves 1,400 steps and may be restricted during high flow.
must_try_food: Hot Mirchi Bajji with steamed spiced tea at the viewpoint canteen.
accessibility: Main viewing gallery is paved and accessible without descending stairs.

name: Belur Chennakeshava & Halebidu Hoysaleshwara
kannada_name: ಬೇಲೂರು ಚೆನ್ನಕೇಶವ ಮತ್ತು ಹಳೇಬೀಡು ಹೊಯ್ಸಳೇಶ್ವರ ದೇವಾಲಯ
description: UNESCO World Heritage Hoysala architectural masterpieces featuring soapstone bracket figures (Madanikas) and unbroken filigree wall friezes.
cultural_note: Authorized government guides are available at the entrance; their historical narrations bring the 900-year-old soapstone carvings to life.
must_try_food: Uppittu (Savory semolina) with filter coffee at local Hassan mess.
accessibility: Step ramps available; temple platform is flat soapstone.

name: Lalbagh Botanical Garden & Bangalore Palace
description: Historic 240-acre botanical haven commissioned by Hyder Ali featuring the famous 1889 Glass House, combined with Tudor-style Bangalore Palace.
best_time_to_visit: Year-round (Republic Day & Independence Day Flower Shows in Jan & Aug)
cultural_note: Lalbagh is directly connected via Namma Metro Green Line (Lalbagh station).
must_try_food: Benne Masala Dosa and filter coffee at Mavalli Tiffin Room (MTR) near Lalbagh Main Gate.
accessibility: Wide paved walking tracks and golf buggies for senior citizens.
